A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mask-Adapter work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. The duplicated supplement appended to v2 is readable and can be matched to existing material.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation evaluations, mask-classification experiments, architectural and training ablations, and SAM integration results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds an experiment comparing alternative block architectures in Appendix B, Table 11.

M1.justification: The proposed architecture, semantic-map aggregation, IoU matcher, mask-consistency loss, two-stage training, and ensemble remain unchanged. The new block alternatives are ablation variants; the proposed model still uses ConvNeXt blocks.

E1.justification: Both versions retain COCO-Stuff and COCO-Panoptic training, LVIS/Grand warmup analyses, ADE20K and Pascal evaluations, and SAM experiments. The added block ablation introduces no new dataset, task, or input scenario.

E2.justification: v2 Table 11 adds ResNet, Transformer, and Swin Transformer blocks as component-level comparators against the selected ConvNeXt block. The end-to-end segmentation baselines and mask-extraction comparators in the existing experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported splits, metrics, training schedules, batch sizes, image resolutions, and ensemble settings remain unchanged. The new block comparison uses the existing ground-truth-mask and FC-CLIP-mask mIoU framework without reporting a different training or testing protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a targeted block-structure ablation comparing ConvNeXt with ResNet, Transformer, and Swin Transformer blocks. Existing analyses of block count, feature fusion, activation-map count, losses, training data, and classification branches are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and training curves without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new ablation follows the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 11 reports FC-CLIP-mask mIoUs of 35.1, 35.0, and 34.9 for ResNet, Transformer, and Swin blocks, versus 35.4 for ConvNeXt. Existing benchmark scores are unchanged. The Adapter mIoU values omitted from revised Table 10 remain in the appended supplement's Table 2. Section 4.2 also adds a 20.5% improvement statement inconsistent with Table 3's 53.0-to-66.7 accuracy comparison, which gives about 25.8% relative improvement.

T1.justification: The task definitions, mask-embedding equations, matching rule, losses, and appendix ensemble formula are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about mask-pooling limitations, Mask-Adapter's effectiveness, robustness training, segmentation improvements, and integration with SAM.

C2.justification: The new block-ablation discussion argues that ConvNeXt performs best and generalizes this to CNN blocks being more suitable for dense prediction. Section 4.2 also explicitly highlights comparisons using the same OpenCLIP backbone. Existing interpretations of generalization, training-data limitations, and SAM's fine-grained masks remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The architecture details, optimizer, hyperparameters, training budgets, hardware, ensemble coefficients, SAM mask-generation instructions, and code/model access statement are retained. The new block ablation supplies no additional implementation specifications or resource-access information.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly credits SparseInst as inspiration for extracting activation maps and adds discussion and citations for PrimitiveNet, YOLO-World, and EVF-SAM. These are limited additions to research positioning; the existing comparisons with related segmentation and adaptation methods remain.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose is retained, with short explanatory additions and an added author. However, v2 appends a second complete A-D supplement after the references, substantially duplicating the document structure and restarting section, table, and figure numbering.

P2.justification: v2 adds the block-ablation table, narrows Table 10, and relocates existing tables through reflow. More substantially, its appended supplement redisplays seven existing figures and three tables with review-copy headers, line numbers, and unresolved citations. These are duplicated displays, not new visual results.

improvement.justification: The added block ablation modestly strengthens the architectural justification, and explicit SparseInst attribution improves research positioning. These benefits coexist with a duplicated supplement containing unresolved citations and a new percentage statement inconsistent with Table 3. The scientific additions are limited, while document coherence and numerical reporting worsen, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
